To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

QTL mapping with a multiple-family approach detected more QTL and explained a larger proportion of genotypic variance than single-family analyses and that QTL-based prediction of Fusarium ear rot resistance in maize is possible with a high-density consensus genetic map and a training set including full sibs.
joint QTL analyses across multiple families and using linkage information detected more QTL and explained a higher proportion of the genotypically determined variance than single-family analyses.
QTL mapping with connected families can detect more QTL than QTL mapping with a single family and that prediction accuracy is tightly associated with the composition of the training set.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an efficient strategy for QTL-based marker-assisted selection (MAS) for Fusarium resistance traits.
the following questions: Which model is most appropriate for QTL mapping of Fusarium resistance?
the development of a robust method for prediction of resistance to Fusarium ear rot in maize.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the choice of the model depends on the size and composition of the TS and the trait under investigation.
Model 3 or Model 4 can be used for QTL analysis and that the TS should contain as many as possible full sibs.
QTL-based prediction ofFusariumresistant genotypes is possible and the best model depends on the number of families and the size of the TS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more closely related the TS and the validation set (VS) the more accurate the predictions of QTL effects in the VS.
Model 3 with a TS of full sibs is recommended for QTL mapping and prediction of resistance toFusarium.

QTL analysis with multiple connected families and Model 3 or Model 4 is recommended for QTL detection and QTL-based prediction, and that prediction accuracy is associated with the kinships of the TS and the validation set.
The main takeaway from our work is that
QTL-based prediction is possible with a large number of connected families and that the choice of the TS is important.
